key_insight: 4th-generation synchrotrons need scintillators that are both faster and brighter than LYSO, and LaBr3/CeBr3 are leading near-term candidates for ultrafast X-ray imaging.
engineering_relevance: Improving scintillator speed, light yield, and UV-to-electrical detection efficiency is critical for enabling MHz-rate phase-contrast imaging and diffraction at APS-U.
method: Characterized candidate scintillator materials for decay time and light output
Integrated detectors and packaging for ultrafast imaging readout
Tested performance in beamline experiments and compared with LYSO/LSO
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that LaBr3 and CeBr3 achieve roughly two-times shorter decay times than LYSO/LSO while maintaining comparable light yield, supporting their suitability for 13 MHz imaging.
watch_item: Many promising scintillators are hygroscopic and emit mostly below 400 nm, so packaging, optical coupling, and high-UV quantum efficiency remain major implementation challenges.
paper_title: Fast and bright scintillators for ultrafast materials dynamics using 4th generation synchrotron
